steps.description:
We will trace the ERC-20 interfaces that Alchemix keeps in `src/interfaces/`.
Starting from the absolute minimum API (`IERC20Minimal`) we will layer on:
- A pure-view metadata extension.
- Minting capability.
- Burning capability.
Along the way you will see exactly which functions/events each interface contributes and how the successive files inherit from OpenZeppelin’s canonical `IERC20`.
`IERC20Minimal` begins with the two canonical ERC-20 events.  They enable off-chain indexers and on-chain logic to react to balance changes and allowance updates.

Lines 20-48 expose the four absolute-core read & write methods:
1. `totalSupply()` – global supply tracker.
2. `balanceOf(account)` – per-holder balance.
3. `transfer(recipient, amount)` – direct move of tokens.
4. `approve(spender, amount)` – grant spending allowance.
`transferFrom(owner, recipient, amount)` finalises the minimal set.  With an approval in place it allows a 3rd party (typically a contract) to move funds on the owner’s behalf.

`IERC20Metadata` is a *pure view* extension ‑ it adds no state-changing behaviour, only human-readable helpers:
- `name()` – full token name.
- `symbol()` – ticker symbol.
- `decimals()` – UI-friendly decimal places.
Everything else is inherited from whichever ERC-20 base the concrete token implements.
`IERC20Mintable` explicitly imports OpenZeppelin’s `IERC20` (not the local minimal version) and then exposes **one** new mutator:
`mint(recipient, amount)` – unrestricted token creation for implementers that need inflation (e.g. staking rewards, synthetic debt).  All standard ERC-20 reads/writes are inherited unchanged from OZ.
`IERC20Burnable` follows the same pattern – import OpenZeppelin and layer burn functionality.

Two overloads are provided:
- `burn(amount)` – holder destroys their own tokens.
- `burnFrom(owner, amount)` – authorised caller burns from another holder, consuming allowance.  This mirrors the approval/transferFrom symmetry seen in the base standard.

Both `Mintable` and `Burnable` reference `../../lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol`. This shows they are *thin* wrappers: all core ERC-20 behaviour is expected to come from the well-audited `OpenZeppelin` implementation; the Alchemix files merely declare additional hooks.

Recap
- `IERC20Minimal` – events + 4 essential functions.
- `IERC20Metadata` – read-only `name`, `symbol`, `decimals`.
- `IERC20Mintable` – adds `mint`, inherits entire `OZ` `IERC20`.
- `IERC20Burnable` – adds `burn` & `burnFrom`, also inherits `OZ` `IERC20`.
This layered approach lets each contract in the system select only the capabilities it needs while still conforming to the broader ERC-20 ecosystem.
